12: class AbsoluteURL {

14:     this.schemePattern = /^[a-z][a-z\d+\-.]*$/i;
15:     this.authorityPrefix = '//';

20:       return false;
21:     }

23:     // A URL is considered absolute only if it begins with "<scheme>://".
24:     // Protocol-relative URLs ("//host") are not treated as absolute to prevent SSRF.
25:     // RFC 3986 defines scheme name as a sequence of characters beginning with a letter and followed
26:     // by any combination of letters, digits, plus, period, or hyphen.

32:       candidate.afterScheme.charAt(1) === this.authorityPrefix.charAt(1);
33:   }

part.text:
Done. The fix is complete and validated.

**Change** (`lib/helpers/isAbsoluteURL.js`): removed the branch that treated protocol-relative URLs (`//host`) as absolute. Previously `isAbsoluteURL('//google.com')` returned `true`, so `buildFullPath` skipped combining the `baseURL`, letting the request URL be resolved as `http://google.com` server-side (SSRF via CVE-2024-39338). Now only `<scheme>://` URLs count as absolute, so protocol-relative paths are safely joined onto the configured `baseURL`.

**Validation**:
- The SSRF regression test `test/unit/regression/SNYK-JS-AXIOS-7361793.js` now passes (it failed before the fix).
- Full unit suite: 188 passing / 1 failing — the single remaining failure ("should support HTTPS protocol") is a pre-existing environment/network issue that also fails at baseline; before the fix the suite had 187 passing / 2 failing, so the only delta is the SSRF test.
- Helper behavior verified against all `isAbsoluteURL.spec.js` expectations (protocol-relative → false, scheme URLs → true, invalid schemes → false) with no test files modified.
